title: [Bug] GUTI parsing corrupts TMSI and mobility registration update reuses the old GUTI
body:
## Bug Description I am testing OAI AMF v2.2.2 with a NAS state-learning harness. The GUTI-based mobility registration update path exposes two defects: incorrect extraction of the existing TMSI, and reuse of the existing identity where the registration procedure requires a newly allocated 5G-GUTI. ### 1. Parsing the existing GUTI corrupts its TMSI For affected values, the AMF converts the received TMSI into a different value, sends that value to the UE in Registration Accept, and then fails to resolve the UE's original NAS context when the UE reconnects using that identity. The next Registration Request consequently triggers a fresh Authentication Request. The root cause is a mismatch between the string producer and parser in `utils/conversions.cpp`: - `tmsi_to_string()` calculates padding from the hexadecimal length of the TMSI, then appends its decimal representation. - `get_tmsi_from_guti()` takes the last 10 characters of the complete GUTI string and parses them as a decimal number. For the observed TMSI `819680250`, the generated decimal suffix has 9 characters. Taking the last 10 characters also consumes the final `1` of the preceding AMF identifier, producing `1819680250`. I observed the following five physical trials sharing the same six-input prefix. Each trial started with a restart of the OAI core, gNB and UE. | Trial | TMSI in Registration Accept
at step 3 | TMSI in Registration Accept
at step 5 | Response to the next
Registration Request | | ----- | ---------------------------------------: | ---------------------------------------: | -------------------------------------------- | | 356 | 819680250 | 1819680250 | Authentication Request | | 357 | 4044545302 | 4044545302 | Registration Accept | | 358 | 778972098 | 1778972098 | Authentication Request | | 1247 | 3993611766 | 3993611766 | Registration Accept | | 1248 | 4151527957 | 4151527957 | Registration Accept | The two changed values each increased by `1,000,000,000`. The resulting identity lookup failure changes the protocol response for the same abstract input sequence, and the learner stopped when the new observation conflicted with its accepted prefix cache. ### 2. Mobility registration update reuses the existing GUTI Trials 357, 1247 and 1248 expose the second defect: their 10-digit TMSIs pass through parsing accurately, and the Registration Accept at step 5 repeats the GUTI already assigned at step 3. The GUAMI and TMSI both stay the same. In the tested source, the GUTI registration handler places the parsed incoming TMSI in `uc->tmsi`; `run_mobility_registration_update_procedure()` then passes that value directly to `RegistrationAccept::Set5gGuti()`. This path echoes the existing identity instead of allocating the new identity required for mobility registration update. The observed exchange proceeds directly to Registration Accept; the new-GUTI requirement therefore applies to that message. These two defects require separate corrections. Parsing should recover the existing identity exactly. Reallocation should create a fresh identity and associate it with the UE context. A changed TMSI produced by field-boundary corruption and an unchanged TMSI produced by accurate parsing are the two observed outcomes of the current path. ## To Reproduce 1. Run OAI AMF v2.2.2 at commit `b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7`, with common-src at `c0dcc9aa70da170b3dcd690a34e704be4199f3fd`. 2. Use a modified UERANSIM UE controlled by a sequence runner to send the following inputs: ```text registrationRequest authenticationResponse securityModeComplete authenticationFailure_71 registrationRequestGUTI registrationRequest ``` `authenticationFailure_71` sends Authentication Failure with cause 71. Before steps 5 and 6, the harness completes a controlled RRC release and sends the next registration as an initial NAS message on a fresh connection. Step 5 uses GUTI; step 6 uses SUCI. Both registration messages carry registration type 2, mobility registration updating. At step 6, the NAS mobile identity is SUCI, while the lower-layer connection carries the UE's stored 5G-S-TMSI in RRC/NGAP. In this harness, sending Registration Complete requires an explicit `registrationComplete` input. The sequence above leaves that action unsent after both steps 3 and 5. The UE processes each Registration Accept and stores its GUTI. The observations concern the identity encoded in the AMF's Registration Accept and its use on the next connection; the reallocation requirement in TS 24.501 §5.5.1.3.4 applies when the AMF sends that acceptance message. 3. Restart the OAI core, gNB and UE before each complete trial. Record the TMSI allocated in the first Registration Accept, the TMSI returned at step 5, and the 5G-S-TMSI carried by the next Initial UE Message. The core assigns a fresh random TMSI in each trial. 4. Compare trials using 9-digit decimal TMSIs whose hexadecimal representation has 8 digits with trials using 10-digit decimal TMSIs. The values `819680250` and `778972098` expose the parsing corruption. The three 10-digit values expose reuse of the previous GUTI at step 5. Check both the GUAMI and TMSI when comparing the identities. 5. Correlate the final response with the AMF's GUTI lookup and security-context handling. The first five abstract outputs in these trials were: ```text authenticationRequest securityModeCommand registrationAccept authenticationRequest registrationAccept ``` The sixth output was `authenticationRequest` for trials 356 and 358, and `registrationAccept` for trials 357, 1247 and 1248. Trials 356–358 executed the six-input word; trials 1247–1248 continued with a seventh `registrationRequestGUTI` after this shared prefix. ## Expected Behavior ### 1. Recover the existing identity accurately Converting an incoming GUTI to its TMSI component should recover the exact 32-bit TMSI encoded in that identity. For example, parsing the existing GUTI containing `819680250` should return `819680250`. This round-trip property should hold across the 32-bit TMSI domain. ### 2. Allocate a new identity for mobility registration update [3GPP TS 24.501 V18.10.0 §5.3.3](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/18.10.00_60/ts_124501v181000p.pdf#page=185) requires a new 5G-GUTI during successful initial registration and mobility registration update (`shall`); periodic registration update carries a recommendation (`should`). [§5.5.1.3.4](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/124500_124599/124501/18.10.00_60/ts_124501v181000p.pdf#page=404) makes GUTI reallocation part of mobility registration update. The new identity must be included in Registration Accept unless it has already been allocated through the generic UE configuration update procedure. In the observed step-5 exchange, Registration Accept is the identity-delivery message. The requirement applies to the complete 5G-GUTI, comprising GUAMI and 5G-TMSI. With the same GUAMI in this deployment, allocating a new GUTI requires a new TMSI value. [TS 33.501 V18.11.0 §6.12.3](https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_ts/133500_133599/133501/18.11.00_60/ts_133501v181100p.pdf#page=115) states the corresponding registration requirements and recommends unpredictable TMSI generation. ### 3. Keep the delivered identity and context indexes synchronized The AMF should associate the newly allocated identity with the intended UE/NAS context before the UE uses it on a subsequent connection. The UE adopts the delivered GUTI, and the AMF manages the old/new identity transition and acknowledgement according to §5.3.3 and the registration procedure rules. The expected flow is: accurately parse the old GUTI, allocate a fresh GUTI, update the context association, and deliver the new identity. Parsing equality and identity renewal are separate requirements at separate stages. ## Environment ```text AMF version: v2.2.2 AMF source commit: b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7 common-src commit: c0dcc9aa70da170b3dcd690a34e704be4199f3fd AMF image: oai-amf:upstream-v2.2.2, built from the official source revision Deployment: cloud VM, Docker Compose Harness: modified UERANSIM gNB/UE, Java bridge, AALPY adaptive L# learner UE/SUL source commit: ec8cdc6be131d4e7579554b87b4168b701751591 Reset method: core, gNB and UE restarted before each complete physical trial Registration Complete: explicit learner input; this sequence leaves it unsent Run ID: 20261014T081619Z-e843c64a Observation window: 2026-10-14 10:52–10:54 UTC and 17:35–17:36 UTC ``` ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files Attach here: [oai-amf-guti-tmsi-config.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33483095/oai-amf-guti-tmsi-config.zip) The archive contains: ```text core.properties oai-ue.yaml oai-gnb.yaml docker-compose-basic-nrf.yaml oai-compose.override.yaml basic_nrf_config.yaml six-input-prefix.seq seven-input-query.seq versions.txt README.md ``` `core.properties` comes from the recorded run directory. The UE, gNB and Compose configuration files come from the deployed paths collected on 15 October 2026. Credential fields use `REDACTED_SET_LOCAL_VALUE`; a reproduction environment should supply matching local UE/subscriber credentials and database initialization data. The actual learner algorithm is recorded in `status.json`; the `ttt` setting in `core.properties` is inherited Java-backend configuration. The run uses these relevant settings: ```text reset_mode=hard rrc_release_policy=before_initial_nas ``` The learner applies whole-query `hard_majority3` voting. The vote over trials 356–358 selected the output sequence ending in Authentication Request by a 2-to-1 majority: trials 356 and 358 returned Authentication Request, and trial 357 returned Registration Accept. Trials 1247–1248 both returned Registration Accept at the same prefix. ### NAS Trace Attach here: [oai-amf-guti-tmsi-trace.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33483127/oai-amf-guti-tmsi-trace.zip) The archive contains: ```text statelearner_trace.jsonl trace-selection.json README.md ``` The trace contains all 32 step records from trials 356, 357, 358, 1247 and 1248: 6, 6, 6, 7 and 7 records respectively. Each selected JSONL record is copied in its original byte representation and source order. `trace-selection.json` maps attachment lines to original trace lines, sessions, steps and UTC timestamps. The per-step records contain the input, abstract response and decoded NAS message bytes. Together with the NGAP decode in the core logs, these are the packet-level evidence provided for this run. The critical TMSI fields are: | Trial | Registration Accept
at step 3 | Registration Accept
at step 5 | Initial UE Message
at step 6 | | ----- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | 356 | `30 DB 53 FA` | `6C 76 1D FA` | `6C 76 1D FA` | | 358 | `2E 6E 2B C2` | `6A 08 F5 C2` | `6A 08 F5 C2` | The first two columns come from downlink NAS identity fields. The last column comes from the AMF's NGAP decode log. The UE receives the changed identity at step 5 and uses it when establishing the next connection. ### Log File Attach here: [oai-amf-guti-tmsi-versions.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33483135/oai-amf-guti-tmsi-versions.txt) [oai-amf-guti-tmsi-logs.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33483134/oai-amf-guti-tmsi-logs.zip) The log archive contains: ```text query-inconsistencies.jsonl accepted-query-cache.jsonl cache-conflicts.jsonl status.json progress.json preflight.json run-manifest.selected.json redaction-manifest.json raw/oai/core-session-356/core.log raw/oai/core-session-357/core.log raw/oai/core-session-358/core.log raw/oai/core-session-1247/core.log raw/oai/core-session-1248/core.log README.md ``` Each session directory also contains `launcher.log` and `session.json`, recording core startup, shutdown and trial boundaries. The three query JSONL files select the six-input word and its seven-input extension. The selected run manifest contains the five corresponding core sessions. The public log copies replace passwords, long-term SIM credentials, derived security keys and the NGAP SecurityKey IE with explicit redaction markers. Original log line numbering remains usable. The redaction manifest identifies the affected files and lines; GUTI/TMSI values, timestamps and protocol-processing events remain available for tracing the defect. Server-side XRES/HXRES diagnostic values also use redaction markers. The NAS trace contains the original test-network messages, including RAND, AUTN and the RES* carried in Authentication Response, for checking the recorded protocol exchange. Trial 356 records the initial allocation: ```text Allocated GUTI 20895010041819680250 (TMSI 819680250) ``` At step 6, the AMF receives the changed identity and follows the fresh-authentication path: ```text Receiving GUTI 208950100411819680250 No existing nas_context with GUTI 208950100411819680250 No Security Context/valid key found Sending Authentication Request with RAND ``` For trial 357, the TMSI remains `4044545302`. The AMF finds the GUTI-associated context, logs `Integrity matched`, and sends another Registration Accept after processing the sixth request. ## System Architecture ```text adaptive learner and Java bridge -> modified UERANSIM UE/gNB -> NAS over RRC and NGAP/N2 -> OAI AMF v2.2.2 built from official source ``` The harness selects uplink NAS messages and records the AMF's downlink responses. The AMF generates the initial TMSI, performs the GUTI conversion, and encodes the Registration Accept containing the corrupted or reused identity. ## Walkthrough First, `tmsi_to_string()` uses the length of the hexadecimal representation to calculate padding, while the appended value comes from `std::to_string(tmsi)`. For `819680250`, the hexadecimal representation is `30DB53FA`, so the padding length is zero and the resulting suffix is the 9-character decimal string `819680250`. The GUTI lookup key has these components: ```text 20895 | 010041 | 819680250 PLMN | AMF ID | TMSI ``` Second, `get_tmsi_from_guti()` takes the final 10 characters. This crosses the field boundary: ```text GUTI string: 20895010041819680250 Last 10 chars: 1819680250 Recovered TMSI: 1819680250 Original TMSI: 819680250 ``` Third, the GUTI registration handler writes the recovered value into `uc->tmsi`. The mobility-registration procedure then uses `uc->tmsi` in `RegistrationAccept::Set5gGuti()`. This places `1819680250` in the downlink identity, as confirmed by the NAS bytes `6C 76 1D FA`. Fourth, the UE stores that GUTI and supplies its 5G-S-TMSI on the next connection. The AMF searches for the changed GUTI, reaches the missing-context path, and initiates authentication. In the 10-digit trials, the conversion returns the original TMSI, the lookup succeeds, and the AMF responds with Registration Accept. Fifth, the same `uc->tmsi` reuse explains the missing identity renewal. For a 10-digit TMSI, the parser accurately recovers the incoming value, and step 5 sends that same value under the same GUAMI. These trials demonstrate accurate parsing together with old-GUTI reuse. For the two affected 9-digit values, the outgoing identity is derived from the corrupted parse. Both cases pass through the same Registration Accept construction rather than a fresh identity-allocation step. Source locations in the tested version: - [common-src `utils/conversions.cpp`, lines 344–360](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-common-src/blob/c0dcc9aa70da170b3dcd690a34e704be4199f3fd/utils/conversions.cpp#L344-L360): string production and TMSI extraction. - [AMF `src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp`, lines 2077–2079](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L2077-L2079): assignment to `uc->tmsi` during GUTI registration. - [AMF `src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp`, lines 5036–5076](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/blob/b2f19d1a4a6f23471f218316b33adc61505035f7/src/amf-app/amf_n1.cpp#L5036-L5076): mobility registration, security-context selection and the outgoing GUTI. The recommended repairs address both stages: 1. Read the existing 32-bit TMSI directly from the decoded structured identity. A string-based solution should use a shared radix and field width across producers, parsers and lookup keys. 2. Allocate a fresh GUTI in the mobility-registration path, associate it with the UE/NAS context, and encode that allocated identity in Registration Accept. Apply the specified old/new identity handling through acknowledgement and subsequent use. Regression tests should cover parsing round-trip equality at hexadecimal and decimal width boundaries, including `268435455`, `268435456`, `999999999` and `1000000000`, plus the two observed failing values. Procedure-level tests should verify fresh identity allocation under a fixed GUAMI, successful context lookup using the delivered identity, and both explicit Registration Complete and subsequent-use-before-acknowledgement cases. ## Related Observation [AMF MR !448](https://gitlab.eurecom.fr/oai/cn5g/oai-cn5g-amf/-/merge_requests/448) and [common-src MR !167](https://gitlab.eurecom.fr/oai/cn5g/oai-cn5g-common-src/-/merge_requests/167) address GUTI-to-TMSI parsing. The corresponding [commit `69081a1`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-common-src/commit/69081a1997cf535da88a2a1137bf50df49568dbd), merged on 17 July 2026, changed extraction from the final 8 characters with hexadecimal conversion to the final 10 characters with decimal conversion. The tested version includes this commit. The present failure concerns the width contract between that decimal parser and `tmsi_to_string()`. The same producer/parser combination is present in [common-src develop at `080ac1a6`](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-common-src/blob/080ac1a66566f7f773e5da0781f7b2f73a85d4e3/utils/conversions.cpp#L344-L360), referenced by AMF develop at `3bb4508b` when checked on 15 October 2026. My earlier [issue #9](https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-amf/issues/9) concerns procedure-state cleanup, authentication-vector reuse and ngKSI allocation after an out-of-order SecurityModeReject. This report tracks GUTI parsing and reallocation defects, with their own TMSI values, source locations and reproduction sequence. Both reports arose from the same NAS state-learning approach.
